mobile.trust_root_accepted_no: No: known to this node, not trusted
mobile.trust_root_accepted_yes: Yes: this node's acceptance reaches it
mobile.trust_root_bundle_title: The seed this node runs on
mobile.trust_root_bundle_not_in_force: This node isn't running on its seed yet, so it has no seed to show for comparison.
mobile.trust_root_state_not_adopted_held: Newer root not adopted: the previous root stays in force ({leg} leg)
mobile.trust_root_state_not_adopted: Root not adopted: this binary's root was refused and no earlier root is held ({leg} leg)
mobile.trust_root_import_not_yet_accepted_why: The root's records are on this node, but this node does not trust it yet. Either it does not hold the root's genesis records yet, and the acceptance is tried again at the next start or import, or its acceptance could not be written.
mobile.trust_root_bounded_none: Nothing in it expires on time alone
mobile.trust_root_charter_value: self-declares this root: {declares} · carries a recovery commitment: {recovery}
mobile.trust_root_drill_signal_note: A signal, not a gate: an old drill never makes a root invalid.
mobile.trust_root_empty: This node reports no roots at all.
mobile.trust_root_halt_latched: LATCHED: the kill switch is pulled
mobile.trust_root_import_allegiance_hint: Optional: the address of the node this seed came from
mobile.trust_root_import_body: Paste a portable seed (mesh-genesis.json) or load the file. The node checks its signatures before it installs anything.
mobile.trust_root_import_not_json: That is not a seed: it is not a JSON object. Nothing was sent.
mobile.trust_root_import_note: Compare before you adopt. The node cannot yet show this seed's fingerprint before installing it (CIRISServer#404), so check out of band with the people who made it that this is their seed.
mobile.trust_root_import_partial: Installed but not accepted: the root is known to this node and not trusted. Adopting again will not help; the acceptance is what failed.
mobile.trust_root_import_signs: This node's owner. The node writes its own acceptance, and the owner's too when the owner's key is on this node.
mobile.trust_root_import_what: It will trust {root}, and every trace:* row it serves will rest on that root.
mobile.trust_root_import_what_unknown: It will trust the root this seed's charter names. This app could not read one from the seed, and the node refuses a seed without one.
mobile.trust_root_intro: The accord is this mesh's default trust root. This shows whether this node trusts it, and any other root it has adopted. You may un-trust the default, adopt another root instead or as well, or run with none (CC 3.2).
mobile.trust_root_kind_family: Family root: keyless; its seats are the holders
mobile.trust_root_kind_unreadable: The node could not evaluate this root
mobile.trust_root_loopback_only: Only a device on this node's own machine can see or change its trust root.
mobile.trust_root_loopback_only_body: The node refuses these requests from anywhere else (CIRISServer#652). Open this card on the computer the node runs on. This is not a report that the node trusts nothing.
mobile.trust_root_not_on_this_node: This node can't report its trust root yet. It needs a CIRISServer with the trust-root routes (#400).
mobile.trust_root_read_failed: Could not read this node's trust root.
mobile.trust_root_read_failed_body: The node was asked and did not answer. This is not a report that it trusts nothing.
mobile.trust_root_refused_bad_bundle: That is JSON, but not a genesis seed. Nothing was installed.
mobile.trust_root_refused_bad_request: The node could not read the request.
mobile.trust_root_refused_bundle_refused: The seed's signatures do not verify. Nothing on this node changed.
mobile.trust_root_refused_install_failed: The seed verified, but its records did not install.
mobile.trust_root_refused_withdraw_failed: The node could not withdraw its acceptance.
mobile.trust_root_refused_bundle_unlabelled: This seed is from before the final genesis. Nothing was installed.
mobile.trust_root_refused_bundle_unlabelled_bod: Its trust records carry no labels saying what each one is for — they were minted before records were labelled. This node would install it as no charter at all, so it refused it. Import a version 3 seed from the final genesis instead.
mobile.trust_root_state_divergent: Altered: the {leg} leg is present and wrong
mobile.trust_root_state_entrenched: Rooted: every check that needs a root can pass
mobile.trust_root_state_pre_genesis: Not rooted yet: the {leg} leg is not installed
mobile.trust_root_state_unknown: The node reported a state this app does not know: {state}
mobile.trust_root_state_unreadable: Unknown: the node could not read its own {leg} leg
mobile.trust_root_untrust_signs: This node, withdrawing its own acceptance. The root's signed records stay, and adopting the seed again restores trust.
mobile.trust_root_untrust_what_last: This is the last root this node trusts. Every check that needs a root fails closed, and the node stops serving trace:* rows.
mobile.trust_root_untrust_what_others: What rests on this root stops. The other root this node trusts stays.
mobile.trust_root_untrust_withdrawn_none: Nothing to withdraw: this node already did not trust it
mobile.trust_root_valid_no: No: at least one check fails
mobile.verify_absent_body: This node does not carry the registry, so it cannot check builds. Another node can.
mobile.verify_absent_title: This node does not verify builds
mobile.verify_not_found_body: The registry answered and holds nothing for this hash.
mobile.verify_revoked_warning: This build has been revoked. Do not use it.
mobile.verify_unavailable_body: This is not the same as 'not registered' — the registry did not answer.
mobile.verify_undeclared_body: This node is older than the capability declaration, so it cannot say. A newer node can verify builds.
mobile.verify_undeclared_title: This node cannot say whether it verifies builds

mobile.files_empty_self: Nothing here yet. What you add stays on your own devices until you share it.

mobile.files_node_too_old_body_versioned: This node is running {version}. Files and notes need ciris-server 0.5.215 or newer. Everything else works normally.
mobile.files_awaiting_key_body: Its bytes are on this device, but the key that opens them hasn't arrived yet. It comes on its own; nothing is wrong.
mobile.files_custody_awaiting_key: This file's key hasn't reached this device yet, so it can't say where the file is. It comes on its own; check again shortly.
mobile.files_too_large: {name} is {size}. Files can be at most {limit} for now.
mobile.files_written_nobody: Added {name}, but only on this device. It reached nobody else.
mobile.files_written_partial: Added {name}. {count} device(s) can't open it yet.
mobile.files_preview_unavailable: No preview for this kind of file here. Save a copy to open it.
mobile.files_save_failed: Couldn't save a copy on this device.
mobile.files_render_awaiting_node: Previews of {format} come from your node, which makes a safe copy first. This node can't do that yet. Save a copy to open it.
mobile.files_render_refused: {format} files are never opened here: they can run code or load things from elsewhere.
mobile.files_render_not_utf8: This text isn't valid UTF-8, so it isn't shown. A guessed rendering could say something the file doesn't.
mobile.files_render_mismatch: This file says it is {declared}, but its bytes are {sniffed}. It isn't shown or saved.
mobile.files_render_polyglot: This {format} file has a second file hidden inside it, so it isn't shown or saved.
mobile.files_save_blocked: Saving isn't offered: this kind of file can run code on your device, or isn't what it says it is.
mobile.files_empty_family: This household has no files yet. What you add here reaches every device in it.
mobile.files_no_household: No household is picked. Choose one in Family › Rules and its files show here.
mobile.files_no_household_yet: You're not in a household yet. Form one in Family › Rules and its files will show here.
mobile.files_unreadable_body: The bytes this node sent don't match the digest it sent with them. They aren't shown or saved.
mobile.files_digest_verified: Verified: SHA-256 {digest} matches what the node sent.
mobile.files_digest_not_sent: Not verified: this node sent no digest with the bytes. That needs ciris-server 0.5.217 or newer.
mobile.files_digest_unknown_alg: Not verified: this node's digest is {alg}, which this app can't check.
mobile.files_policy_builtin: This node publishes no render policy, so this app's built-in limits apply.
mobile.notes_empty: No notes yet. Notes stay in Just me, on your own devices.
mobile.files_custody_error: Couldn't find out where this file is.
mobile.files_custody_node_too_old: This node can't say which of your devices a file is on. That needs a newer ciris-server.
mobile.files_custody_node_too_old_versioned: This node is running {version}, which can't say which of your devices a file is on. That needs a newer ciris-server.
mobile.files_custody_no_devices: This node named none of your devices for this file.
mobile.files_custody_on_at_least_n_of_m: On at least {n} of your {m} devices. For {unknown} of them, this device has no way to know yet.
mobile.files_custody_copies_not_observable: Copies elsewhere can't be counted for your own and family files. That is by design, and it doesn't mean there is only one copy.
mobile.files_custody_footnote_receipts: A receipt shows a device received the file. It doesn't show the device still has it: removing a file from a device doesn't take its receipt back yet.
mobile.files_custody_footnote_remove: Once removing a copy is available, it will never delete the last remaining copy of a file that you haven't withdrawn.
mobile.files_custody_footnote_receipts_unsuppor: Small files (1 MiB or less) don't carry receipts yet, so another device's copy shows as unknown, not as missing.
mobile.files_custody_author_here: This device. It collects the receipts, so this is the fullest answer.
mobile.files_custody_author_elsewhere: {device}. That device collects the receipts, so it has the fullest answer.
mobile.files_custody_other_keys: Receipts from keys that aren't your devices

mobile.identity_release_signer: Your own key, as a withdrawal of your ownership

mobile.contact_code_without_transport: Not in this code yet: {devices}. A device can go in once it has a network address here, after its node next starts.
mobile.contact_code_disclosure: Anyone with this code can ask to add you, and can see which of your devices it names.
mobile.contact_code_private_note: Only reachable devices can go in a code. Your other devices are private.
mobile.contact_code_list_reloaded: Your list of reachable devices was reloaded. The code below is for the devices that are reachable now.
mobile.contact_code_unreachable: No one can find you with this yet: none of your devices is reachable. Make this device reachable, or share a code that includes it.
mobile.contact_code_made_reachable: This device is reachable now. Its network address is announced the next time its node starts.

mobile.contact_code_error: Could not get your contact code.
mobile.contact_code_node_too_old: This node can't make a contact code yet. It needs ciris-server 0.5.218 or newer.
mobile.accord_binding_reactivated: reactivated · the named constitutional halt is ENDED — this is the opposite of a halt, not a notice.

mobile.accord_coscrub_save_failed: Couldn't save to {dir} (this platform may not support file writes).
mobile.accord_coscrub_copied: Copied the co-scrub partial for {key} to the clipboard.
mobile.accord_supersede_desc: Admits the successor's completed 2-of-3 canonical record, then tombstones {key} as superseded by it — the canonical set is never empty in between. Needs the 2-of-3 accord proposal that authorises the rotation.
mobile.accord_supersede_record_hint: Paste the successor's completed, 2-of-3-scrubbed key record
mobile.accord_supersede_not_json: That is not a key record — nothing was sent.
mobile.accord_supersede_who: {old} is retired; {new} takes its place as a canonical server.
mobile.accord_supersede_who_unnamed: {old} is retired; the pasted record names no key_id, so the node decides the successor.
mobile.accord_supersede_what: The successor is admitted first, then {old} is tombstoned as superseded — nodes that bootstrap from the canonical set stop dialing it. This cannot be undone here.
mobile.accord_supersede_signs: The 2-of-3 accord proposal {digest} authorises it; the node re-tallies its holder signatures. Your yes sends it under the owner session.
mobile.constitutional_halt_active_invocation: ACTIVE HALT — node execution halted by invocation {id}
mobile.constitutional_halt_active: ACTIVE HALT — node execution is halted
mobile.constitutional_killswitch_unknown: Kill-switch status UNKNOWN — the node did not answer. This is not a report that it is disarmed.
mobile.constitutional_family_desc_threshold: A {m}-of-{n} human kill-switch family: each holder carries a primary SEAT and a cold SPARE. FIPS YubiKey + ML-DSA hardware custody.
mobile.constitutional_family_desc: A human kill-switch family: each holder carries a primary SEAT and a cold SPARE. FIPS YubiKey + ML-DSA hardware custody.
mobile.constitutional_reserved_desc: Only certified accord_holder identities may emit accord:* namespace attestations. All attempts to forge constitutional claims are refused fail-closed by node verification.

mobile.manage_consent_revoke_unsupported: This node can't withdraw consent yet (needs ciris-server 0.5.218).
mobile.manage_consent_revoke_needs_grant: Revoke names one grant, and this node doesn't list its peering grants yet, so it works on a grant set up here in this session.
mobile.manage_consent_withdrawn: Withdrawn. The node recorded your withdrawal ({id}).
mobile.consent_withdraw_signs_value: You. The node signs the withdrawal with your key, never its own.
mobile.consent_remaining_row: Still active: this node wrote it before you signed, so it can't be withdrawn here.
mobile.contacts_remove_fact_stops_value: Your consent to share with them. Your messages and shared records stop replicating to them.
mobile.contacts_removed: Removed {who}. Your consent to them is withdrawn.
mobile.contacts_remove_remaining_body: You withdrew {count} grant(s). The grants below are still active.
mobile.contacts_remove_remaining_row: Still active: written by this node before you signed your contacts, so it can't be withdrawn here
mobile.contacts_remove_unsupported: This node can't remove contacts yet (needs ciris-server 0.5.218).
mobile.community_section_body: Groups you belong to by choice. Each one runs by its own rule for who may change it, and that rule is on the record.
mobile.community_section_body_affiliations: Groups you belong to because your role requires it: work, an institution, an office. The same machinery as a community, at the affiliations tier.
mobile.community_empty: You are not in any community yet. Found one and add the people you already have as contacts.
mobile.community_empty_affiliations: You are not in any affiliation yet.
mobile.community_not_on_this_node: This node doesn't serve communities yet. It needs CIRISServer 0.5.216 or later.
mobile.community_read_failed_body: The node was asked and did not answer. This is not a report that you have none.
mobile.community_act_failed: The node did not make that change.
mobile.community_row_pending: A change is waiting for signatures
mobile.community_create_members: Who is in it from the start
mobile.community_create_members_none: You have no contacts yet. You can found it alone and add people once they are contacts.
mobile.community_create_quorum_m: How many of the {n} must sign
mobile.community_protocol_founder_only_body: One founder's signature changes the roster. An appointed moderator may also add or remove a plain member.
mobile.community_protocol_unanimous_body: Every active member signs a change, except the person a removal is about.
mobile.community_protocol_majority_body: More than half of the active members sign a change.
mobile.community_protocol_quorum_body: That many members sign a change. It must be more than half, so two separate groups can never both decide.
mobile.community_protocol_other_body: This rule came from another node. It can be read here, and this node cannot change the room under it.
mobile.community_detail_not_found: This node has no community by that id that you are in. It may have been dissolved, or you may have been removed; the node gives both the same answer on purpose.
mobile.community_detail_pending_note: A change is waiting for signatures below.
mobile.community_role_body: A role is the roster's word: founder, member, or your own. It is not a duty. Moderating is a duty someone is given, and a role does not grant it.
mobile.community_moderators_none: No appointed moderator is on record.
mobile.community_moderators_unreadable: This node could not read who holds the moderation duty here. That is not a report that nobody does.
mobile.community_moderators_not_sent: This node did not send who holds the moderation duty here.
mobile.community_appoint_unavailable: Appointing a moderator for this room is not built here. The duty conferral this app has is the accord's, not a founder's.
mobile.community_moderation_pick_none: You are not in any community of more than two people.
mobile.community_moderation_pick_unreadable: Could not read your communities. Type the community key above instead.
mobile.community_affiliations_terms_unavailable: What this body has declared it can do with what you put here (classification, retention, lawful access) has no route yet (CIRISServer#649). Joining does not show it, and this app will not guess it.
mobile.community_confirm_leave_what: You are removed from its roster and receive nothing new from it. What you already received stays with you. Only a member can add you back.
mobile.community_confirm_dissolve_what: Every member is removed and the room's key is rotated. Nobody is left who can change it again. This cannot be undone.
mobile.community_confirm_remove_what: They are removed from the roster and the room's key is rotated, so they receive nothing new. What they already received stays with them.
mobile.community_confirm_signs_leave: You, with your own key. Leaving is always your own act and never waits on the rule.
mobile.community_confirm_signs_governed: You, with your own key, under the room's rule ({rule}). If the rule needs more signatures, nothing changes until they are collected.
mobile.community_pending_how: The node keeps nothing until this is finished. Send the change below to the others; each signs it on their own node and sends back a signature, which you add here.
mobile.community_cosign_title: Sign a change someone sent you
mobile.community_cosign_body: Paste the change another member sent. This node checks it still describes the room, then you sign it with your own key. Nothing is applied here; send the signature back to them.
mobile.community_cosign_done: Signed. Send this back to the person collecting signatures.
mobile.community_paste_malformed: That is not a change or a signature this app can read. Paste exactly what was sent.
mobile.community_roster_empty: You are not in any room at this tier yet. Found one from this circle's Rules.
mobile.community_roster_pending_note: A roster change is waiting for signatures. Finish it from this circle's Rules.
mobile.community_limit_widened_reads: Someone added after a room was founded is listed and sealed to, and cannot read its messages yet (CIRISPersist#907).
mobile.community_group_book_unavailable: Who admitted each member, and what changed when, is not served yet (CIRISServer#650). This is who is in it now.
mobile.community_member_late: Added after founding: cannot read yet
mobile.community_add_body: They must already be a contact. Under the room's rule this may need more signatures before it takes effect.
mobile.community_chats_empty: No rooms here yet. A chat with a contact appears here once it is opened.
mobile.community_chat_room_unopenable: A room of more than two cannot be opened here yet; the chat screen opens a room only through a contact.
mobile.community_chat_not_a_contact: Not a contact any more. The room is still there and nothing can leave it.

mobile.login_new_account_observer: An account this node has never seen would be let in as an observer, not as the owner.
mobile.login_new_account_claims: This node has no owner yet: the first account to sign in becomes its owner.

mobile.skill_remove_effect: Its tools leave this agent and its adapter folder is deleted. To have it again, you import it again.
mobile.skill_remove_actor: You, as this agent's admin. The agent records no signature for a removal.

mobile.wallet_transfer_unknown: The send was requested but no answer came back. Check the balance and history before sending again — it may already have gone.

mobile.setup_announce_not_offered_minor: Making this device visible to the federation isn't offered to under-18 or undeclared accounts yet. People you're connected to can still reach you.
mobile.setup_templates_error: The agent's templates couldn't be read, so the default template will be used.
mobile.setup_adapters_error: The agent's optional features couldn't be read. That doesn't mean there are none.

mobile.setup_tool_disclosure_error: What these features let the agent do couldn't be read. That doesn't mean they grant nothing.

mobile.server_no_recent: No previous connections on this device.

mobile.settings_location_needs_agent: Where you are is stored by an AI agent, and this device runs a node without one, so it can't be set here yet.
mobile.llm_settings_disable_ciris_reversible: You can turn CIRIS services back on here later; it takes effect after the agent restarts.
mobile.llm_settings_reenable_after_restart: Turning this back on takes effect after the agent restarts

mobile.manage_nodes_unverified: This list could not be checked against the nodes you own. It shows only this device and any node you added in this session. That does not mean you own nothing else.
mobile.moderation_named_none: No community asked about yet. Type a community key and press Check.
mobile.moderation_named_error: Could not ask this node about that community ({detail}). This is NOT a report that it has a moderator.
mobile.moderation_named_not_on_this_node: This node can't say who moderates a community yet: it has no named-moderator route. This is NOT a report that the community has a moderator.
mobile.moderation_verdict_unknown: The node answered a verdict this app does not know ({verdict}). Treat the community as not cleared to operate.
mobile.moderation_candidate_row: Candidate: {candidate}. The node names who was chosen, but not yet the track record that chose them.
mobile.data_erase_title: Erase an agent's traces on this node
mobile.data_erase_desc: This node keeps the traces that agents send it. You can erase every trace one agent filed here. This is the only erasure this node can do today, so read what it reaches and what it does not.
mobile.data_erase_reaches: Every trace filed under that agent id on this node, and the model calls inside them. Detections made from them keep their numbers and lose the link to the agent.
mobile.data_erase_not_reached: Chats, notes, files, consent records, anything inside a signed envelope, and every copy already sent to another node or to CIRISLens. Nothing this node records today can be erased (CIRISPersist#914).
mobile.data_erase_self_blocked: Not possible from this app yet. The node erases a person only on a request that person signs, and this app does not sign (CIRISServer#677). Erasing traces does not erase you.
mobile.data_erase_agent_id_placeholder: The agent id the traces were filed under
mobile.data_erase_reason_placeholder: Why these traces are being erased (the node records it)
mobile.data_erase_confirm_title: Erase these traces from this node?
mobile.data_erase_fact_erased: Every trace filed under {hash} on this node, and its model calls. Detections lose the link.
mobile.data_erase_fact_kept: Everything else this node holds, and every copy already on another node or in CIRISLens.
mobile.data_erase_fact_signer: Your owner session on this node. This cannot be undone.
mobile.data_erase_nothing: This node holds no traces under that id. Nothing was erased.
mobile.data_erase_partial: The node did not say the traces were erased
mobile.data_erase_partial_body: Treat them as still there, and try again.
mobile.data_erase_not_on_this_node: This node can't erase traces. It needs a CIRISServer that serves /v1/federation/erase-agent-traces.
mobile.data_erase_refused_signin: Sign in as this node's owner to erase traces
mobile.data_erase_refused_owner: Only this node's owner can erase traces
mobile.data_erase_failed_body: Nothing is known to have been erased.
mobile.data_erase_result_receipt_none: None. This node does not issue one; it records the erasure in its own record as hard_case:trace_erasure.
mobile.data_receipts_desc: When this agent deletes someone's data it can sign a receipt. Paste a receipt here to check its signature against this agent's key.
mobile.data_receipts_none_issued: This agent does not issue receipts yet. Its signer exists and nothing calls it (CIRISAgent#1207), so a completed deletion request has no receipt.
mobile.data_receipts_public_key_unread: The key id was read; the public key could not be downloaded.
mobile.data_receipts_not_on_this_agent: This agent can't check receipts. It needs a CIRISAgent that serves /v1/verification.
mobile.data_receipt_unreadable: This is not a receipt this app can read
mobile.data_receipt_valid: Checks: signed by this agent's key
mobile.data_receipt_key_not_current: Signed by a key this agent no longer uses. It checks only against its current key, so this receipt reads as not checking even if it is genuine.
mobile.manage_consent_msg_ratified: Bilateral replication ratified — both grants present.
mobile.manage_consent_msg_partial: Partial: this device → peer {a}, peer → this device {b}.
mobile.manage_consent_traces_elsewhere: Whether this agent's anonymous reasoning traces are sent to the CIRIS community is decided on the Data card (My things › Everything I shared › Data), where the setting is read back. It used to be written from here as well; one act now has one door.
mobile.consent_stream_fact_who_value: You — your consent record with this agent (currently {from}).
mobile.consent_stream_leave_partnered: Your partnership ends and your stream becomes {stream}. This is not an undo: the agent severs your identity at once and lets what it learned from you fade over 90 days; anonymised safety patterns may be kept.

agent.title: Agent (Self)
agent.subtitle: The agent itself — implicit self at every scale.
agent.identities_description: The agent's own identity key — the federation address it signs every contribution with. Friendly name from local config; key_id from CIRISEdge.
agent.trust_description: Self-trust is foundational. The Recursive Golden Rule has no exemption clauses — what the agent demands of others, it must hold itself to.
agent.policies_description: Self-applying policies: identity rotation cadence, attestation refresh, what the agent is willing to sign at this scope.

family.title: Family
family.subtitle: Other CIRIS occurrences sharing this operator's identity.
family.identities_description: Sibling occurrences (different runtime instances of the same agent) and their occurrence_id. Friendly name from operator config.
family.trust_description: Family members share the operator's signing key by default — direct trust is the baseline. Shared shutdown / wakeup decisions per multi-occurrence coordination.
family.policies_description: Cross-occurrence policies: shared task claiming, multi-occurrence safety bounds, decision quorum for family-scope actions.

local_community.title: Local Community
local_community.subtitle: Locally-trusted peers — home channel, household, single guild.
local_community.identities_description: Peers explicitly trusted by the operator. Friendly name from contact book; key_id from announcement table.
local_community.trust_description: Direct trust extended by the operator. May be revoked at any time. Local-scope contributions stay in the local cohort and are not federation-published.
local_community.policies_description: Per-community policies: who may invite, what content classes are admitted, how disputes are resolved at this scope.

global_communities.title: Global Communities
global_communities.subtitle: Cross-community affinity groups the agent has joined.
global_communities.identities_description: Affiliated communities (cooperatives, professional bodies, mutual-aid networks) the agent participates in. Friendly name from accord_holder registry; key_id otherwise.
global_communities.trust_description: Trust is transitive through community membership. Each community has its own admission criteria and its own attestation discipline.
global_communities.policies_description: Affiliation-scope policies: which communities the agent will accept guidance from, conflict-resolution between competing affiliations.

global_commons.title: Global Commons
global_commons.subtitle: The federation as the universal layer — humanity, ecology, the substrate itself.
global_commons.identities_description: All identities visible at federation scope, including humanity_accord halt-authority holders, accord_holder principals, and the broader peer pool.
global_commons.trust_description: Trust at the universal scope is conferred by the federation's own attestation discipline. The Recursive Golden Rule binds every principal — including CIRIS L3C — at this scope.
global_commons.policies_description: Federation-wide constitutional bounds: humanity_accord halt-authority, accord_holder reserved prefixes, locality:decision quorum sizing.

commons.title: The Commons
commons.description: Federation contribution cards: accord files, safety tests, behavior witnesses, rubric updates, recantations, delegations. Each carries polarity, confidence, witness diversity, and audit-chain lineage resolved through Edge's ContentFetch transport.

participate.title: Participate
participate.description: Federation needs registry — agents register what they need (rubric review, safety witness, delegation scope) as need:{domain}:{kind} attestations; other agents see, score, and respond.

environment_graph.title: Environment Graph
environment_graph.description: Lens-derived environment graph — manifold conformity scores per cohort, distributive access measurements, correlated-action detections. The graph layer above the federation directory that the agent reasons against during decision-making.

delegation.title: Delegation
delegation.description: Delegation graph: scopes delegated to and from this agent, with grant timestamps, evidence refs, and any withdrawal chains. One of the 4 structural primitives — co-owned with the federation directory.

trust_topology.title: Trust Topology
trust_topology.description: Federation trust graph — peers as nodes, trust grants as edges (direct / delegated / adversarial), edge color = transport reachability, node size = aggregate trust weight.

constitutional.title: Constitutional
constitutional.description: Accord-holder identity surface — the one constitutional asymmetry per FSD-002 §4.1. Only identity_type=accord_holder keys may emit accord:* attestations; this screen shows current holders, their issued accord-prefix emissions, and the reserved-prefix enforcement audit.

standing.refused: This node holds a live de-admission of this key that it authored itself, so the key's next write into this node's corpus is refused at the substrate's own door.
standing.unreadable: This node could not read its own admission state for this key, so it does not know whether that key's writes are refused. This is NOT 'admitted' — do not render it as one.

descend.bounded_unsupported: A time-bounded judgement cannot drive an unbounded eviction. The substrate's only actor-keyed descent takes the whole corpus, which would destroy the history this bound deliberately leaves standing. The time-bounded removal that IS implemented is de-admission with a history bound.
descend.not_reached: The selected attestation rows themselves are not descended. Every payload carrier on this substrate is sealed inside its own signature, so its bytes cannot be dropped without making the row read as forged; erasability is decided at mint and nothing minted today is erasable.

enforcement.accept_writes: This node stops refusing the named keys' writes: the de-admission it authored is withdrawn and the substrate admits their next write again. Both the de-admission and this withdrawal survive as readable history.
enforcement.annotate: A signed judgement with no effect until a reader honours it. Nothing is withheld, throttled or removed.
enforcement.deadmit: A signed revocation on the ordinary append-only plane. It is evidence a reader folds, not a door that slams: signature verification, the replication cursors and row ingest all deliberately keep working, because refusing a compromised key's older rows would destroy the evidence needed to adjudicate the compromise.
enforcement.descend: Irreversible by design. Descent never terminates at zero — the blur and the tombstone survive — but what was shed is not coming back.
enforcement.quarantine: A signed marker, not a command: nothing is deleted and nothing is rewritten. This node's serve paths stop handing the named keys' rows and blobs to peers; a peer that folds differently simply does not receive them from us.
enforcement.re_admit: Recorded as an attributed reversal. The revocation row survives and every reader still folds it: restrictions compose and leniencies do not, and no layer of this substrate exposes an un-revoke.
enforcement.refuse_writes: This node refuses the named keys' next write into its own corpus, at the substrate's own door and before any other gate runs. It is LOCAL by design: no node decrees another node's admission set, because a globally-effective de-admission would itself be a censorship weapon. Isolation of a genuine abuser is emergent — it arrives when many nodes independently reach the same conclusion — and is never decreed from here.
enforcement.throttle: Recorded as an attributed judgement only. This substrate has no recipient-authored per-key admission budget: the peer write quota is a fixed runaway-loop backstop, not a policy surface a throttle can key on. Nothing changes what this node accepts from the named keys.

preview.note: This is exactly what a commit will act on. Present the selection hash with the commit; if the selection has changed, the commit refuses.
preview.window_in_application: The time window is applied by this node, not by the substrate query: the general attestation read does not honour the window axis. The page bound is applied first, so a windowed selection can come back short.

quarantine.not_withheld: This key is not currently withheld here, so there is nothing to release.

reader.advisory: An issued judgement is advisory to each reader. `reader_fold` is what THIS reader's policy makes of what it holds; `node_fold` is what this node's serve paths do today, which is to honour every marker the substrate admitted. They can differ, and when they do the difference is the substrate gap: there is no reader-policy hook in the serve-side fold, so a decline is recorded and reported and does not yet stop this node withholding.

decision.declined: This reader refused this judgement. A normal outcome: an issued judgement is advisory to each reader, and refusing one is the property the whole rung exists for.
decision.honoured_by_subscription: No explicit decision was recorded; this reader subscribes to the signer, so the judgement is honoured by policy.
decision.honoured_explicit: This reader adopted this judgement deliberately.
decision.undecided_unsubscribed: This reader does not subscribe to the signer and has recorded no decision. The judgement is not honoured, and that is nobody's decision yet — which is a different fact from having refused it.

standing.decided: Every judgement this node holds about that subject is listed with what this reader does about it.
standing.none_held: This node holds no judgement about that subject. Nobody has judged it here — which is not the same as this node being unable to say.
standing.unreadable: This reader could not read its own state, so it cannot say what it honours. This is NOT 'no judgements' and NOT 'nothing withheld' — an unreadable policy rendered as an empty one silently drops every restriction it carried.

refusal.attribution_absent: delegation_id is required. An action that does not carry its own authority cannot be told from an unauthorized one once the actor is gone.
refusal.authority_not_a_delegation: The named delegation id is not a delegates_to row.
refusal.authority_not_the_owner: A self-directed act is the owner's own. The named delegation carries the right scope but was not issued by this node's responsible party, and a third party's serve grant is not the owner's.
refusal.authority_not_to_actor: The named delegation was not granted to this node, so this node is not the party it authorizes.
refusal.authority_scope_absent: The named delegation does not carry the scope this operation requires. Another delegation from the same issuer might, but the act would then record an authority it was not taken under.
refusal.authority_scope_unreachable: No live delegation chain carrying the scope this operation requires reaches this node from that issuer. Authority is re-derived from this node's own verified state, never taken from the request.
refusal.authority_unresolved: The named delegation is not a row this node holds, so its scope cannot be checked. This node does not act on an authority it cannot verify.
refusal.bad_request: The request body could not be parsed.
refusal.community_absent: community_id is required: a quarantine is filed under a community's authority, and a marker that names no community names no authority.
refusal.deadmission_gate_dormant: This node has not declared its own identity to the substrate, so the de-admission gate is dormant: the row would be written and would refuse nothing. Refused rather than handed back as done — a sanction gate that silently does nothing is worse than no gate, because an operator will believe de-admission works. This is a node-configuration fault, not a fault of the request.
refusal.deadmission_gate_foreign_identity: The identity this node signs as and the identity the de-admission gate compares writers against are two different keys, so a de-admission signed here would never be folded as this node's own and would refuse nothing. This is a node-configuration fault, not a fault of the request.
refusal.judgement_subjectless: That judgement names no subject, so honouring or declining it would change nothing about anyone. This node does not record a decision it cannot apply.
refusal.judgement_unresolved: That judgement is not a row this node holds, so this reader has nothing to decide about. A reader decides what it HOLDS; it does not pre-refuse what it has never seen.
refusal.node_unowned: This node has no responsible party (owner-binding), so it performs no graded admin operation on anyone's behalf. Claim ownership first.
refusal.not_a_judgement: That row is not a judgement this rung can decide about. Tier R is the reader's policy over other parties' JUDGEMENTS, and an ordinary attestation is not one.
refusal.not_owner: Graded admin operations require the owner (SYSTEM_ADMIN) role.
refusal.preview_hash_mismatch: What you previewed is not what would execute — the selection has changed since the preview. Re-run the preview and ratify the new hash.
refusal.quorum_insufficient: This operation is irreversible and takes a quorum of distinct authorities, not one delegation chain. Two chains from the same root are one authority wearing two hats.
refusal.reason_absent: reason is required. An action with no recorded reason is indistinguishable from an unauthorized one once the actor is gone.
refusal.selection_unpredicated: The selection carries no predicate at all, which means the whole corpus. Name what you are acting on.
refusal.session_absent: No session token was presented. Graded admin operations are owner-only.
refusal.session_invalid: That session is invalid or expired.
refusal.store_unavailable: The substrate could not be read.
refusal.subject_absent: subject_key_id is required: a reader fold is about one subject's judgements, and an unnamed subject is every subject.

refuse_writes.already_refused: This key is already de-admitted here, so nothing was written and the standing is unchanged.
refuse_writes.not_reached: It unwrites nothing. Rows these keys already wrote here are untouched and still served — quarantine is the op that stops serving them. Rows that already replicated to peers are not recalled and cannot be. The keys are not removed, their signatures still verify, and they go on writing to every other node, including this node's peers, from which those rows may arrive here again by replication. One exemption survives on purpose so that a node can always lift its own denial, and it does not ask who is writing: a de-admitted key may still write de-admission rows here (CIRISPersist#608).
refuse_writes.reversal: Reversible, and the reversal reaches the substrate rather than merely recording a change of mind: POST /v1/admin/accept-writes withdraws the de-admission and the key's writes are admitted here again. Two of this ladder's reversals reach the substrate — releasing a quarantine, which restores what this node SERVES, and this one, which restores what it ACCEPTS. Both rows survive and stay readable: 'refused and then re-admitted' is not the same fact as 'never refused'.

reversal.evidence_only: The original row survives and is still folded by every reader. This reversal is recorded evidence, not an undo — the substrate exposes no un-revoke.
reversal.substrate: The substrate state is reversed: this node stops withholding the key's rows.
reversal.symmetric: Nothing in the substrate is reversed because nothing in the substrate enforced the original judgement. Both acts are recorded evidence.

self.distinct_zeroes: Three of the four standings are zeroes and they mean different things: never declared, declared and lifted, and could not be read. Render them differently.

enforcement.compelled: Recorded on its own axis, as its own act. This is a statement about force applied from OUTSIDE the mesh, and by itself it changes nothing this node does — deliberately. A compelled node may be made to keep serving, to stop, or to hand something over; folding any of those into 'this node stopped accepting' would destroy the only signal a downstream party has for telling a choice from a compulsion.
enforcement.shed: Recorded as this node's own attributed declaration, and nothing more. The mesh-config plane that would carry a load ceiling is authored by trust roots, and this node runs no consumer of the folded values yet, so no loop changes what it carries. What changes is the record: an operator, a peer or a later audit can tell that this node chose to carry less, under whose authority, and when.
enforcement.stop_accepting: Recorded as this node's own attributed declaration that it is taking on nothing new. Nothing in this substrate enforces it: the receive plane is peer-blind and the per-peer write quota is a fixed runaway-loop backstop, not a policy surface a stop can key on. The declaration is the artifact — and it is the one a peer reads to stop offering.

lift.compelled: Recorded as a distinct act: a compulsion that ENDED is not a compulsion that never happened. The declaration it lifts survives, and both remain readable.
lift.voluntary: Recorded as a distinct act. The declaration it lifts survives, and both remain readable — 'declared and lifted' is not 'never declared'.

self.partition: Every act on this rung is local: the owner-binding walk, the ledger write and this read all touch this node's own database and nothing else. It is the only rung available while partitioned — every other rung has to reach someone.

standing.in_force: This node declared this and has not lifted it.
standing.lifted: This node declared this and lifted it again. That is not the same fact as never having declared it.
standing.never_declared: This node has never declared this. That is not the same fact as having declared and lifted it, and not the same fact as being unable to read.
standing.unreadable: The record could not be read, so this node does not know its own standing on this axis. This is NOT 'nothing in force' — do not render it as one.

failed.local: This node could not build the revocation. Nothing was changed, and this is not an authority refusal — the act was never put to the substrate. The stage that failed is in `error`.
failed.substrate: The revocation could not be written. This is not an authority refusal — the substrate did not complete the act. The technical detail is in `error`.

refused.no_slash_grant: This node is not authorised to de-admit someone else's key. Revoking a key that is not your own is a moderation act, and it needs the `slash` duty granted to this node by a trust root it accepts. Nothing was changed. Ask an accord holder to delegate `slash` for federation duties to this node, then run the same selection again — the preview hash still applies.
refused.node_identity_unset: This node has no federation identity yet, so it cannot sign a revocation or resolve whether it holds the authority to issue one. Complete node setup first.

commons_surface.asymmetry: One member raises the brake; the cohort must agree to lift it. Raising protection is unconditional and costs one signature; undoing somebody else's costs the cohort's own threshold, and the escalated undo can never fall below an absolute floor no policy string may lower.

ballot.admitted: The ballot is on the record. It has NO force on its own: its price is paid at read time against a denominator that does not exist yet when it is cast — whether the pool ever reaches the escalated threshold depends on who else answers. A member may change their mind; the latest ballot governs.

dismissal.admitted: The objection is lifted for the count. The threshold is re-derived from this node's own roster on every later read, so a dismissal that stops clearing a grown roster stops suppressing — and the protection it removed comes back.

commons_surface.dry_run: Nothing was signed and nothing was submitted. These are the exact canonical bytes each co-signer must sign for their scrub to count on the real submission — the m-of-n is over these bytes and no others.

escalation.awaiting: The appointed moderators may still answer, or they have already ruled in time. Escalation has not opened.
escalation.not_adopted: This community declared no steward tier, so there is no moderator deadline and no escalation. Silence changes nothing here.
escalation.nothing_to_escalate: A steward tier is declared and no live objection is waiting on it. Nobody was silent, because nothing was asked.
escalation.open: The duty-holders did not answer in time, and the decision has passed to those who did. The threshold now counts RESPONDENTS rather than the whole roster — which is what lets a quiet community still resolve — floored so that 'reachable' never degrades to 'one person decides'.

objection.admitted: The objection is on the record. It is a MARKER, not a command: nothing was changed by its arrival, and it replicates on the ordinary attestation plane so a peer that was partitioned during the window still counts it when it arrives. One member is enough to raise it; lifting it costs the cohort's own threshold.

outcome.dismissed: Those who answered ruled that this objection does not stand, and it is suppressed for the count.
outcome.not_escalated: Escalation did not open for this objection.
outcome.unresolved: Escalation is open and undecided: too few have answered, or neither side has reached the threshold. Nothing changes — the objection stands exactly as it did.
outcome.upheld: Those who answered ruled that this objection stands.

refusal.action_absent: action_id is required. An objection names a row in the commons; one that names nothing can never be counted.
refusal.action_unknown: This node holds no such action, so a row naming it would be filed where no fold will ever count it. The substrate refuses the same case at its own door.
refusal.actor_recused: The author of the action does not vote on the objection to their own act.
refusal.bad_now: The read-time instant must be an RFC 3339 timestamp.
refusal.ballot_predates_action: A judgement cannot be older than the thing it judges.
refusal.canonicalize_failed: The row's canonical bytes could not be produced, so there is nothing a co-signer could sign.
refusal.cohort_absent: cohort_key_id is required: it names whose roster and whose declaration govern the count.
refusal.cohort_not_a_commons: The `self` cohort has no roster to be a quorum over — its members are one identity's own devices — so it has no commons to police.
refusal.cohort_unknown: That cohort does not resolve on this node, so there is no roster and no declaration to judge this by. Authority must come from local verified state.
refusal.cohort_unrecognized: That is not a rostered cohort. Objections live in a family, a community or an affiliations group.
refusal.dimension_mismatch: That row was offered at the wrong door for what it carries.
refusal.dismissal_quorum_short: Fewer distinct verified roster members co-signed than the cohort's threshold demands. The counted and required numbers are beside this message.
refusal.duplicate_objection: You already hold a live objection against this action. One member is one objection — otherwise a single member could reach the threshold alone.
refusal.grounds_absent: grounds is required. An objection raised for no recorded reason is indistinguishable from one raised for a bad one — and grounds are recorded, never interpreted.
refusal.malformed_envelope: The row is missing a reference the count needs.
refusal.node_unowned: This node has no responsible party (owner-binding), so it neither reads nor speaks in anyone's commons on their behalf. Claim ownership first.
refusal.not_a_cohort_member: Only a member of this cohort may speak in its commons. This is the only test the protective side applies — and the reason a stranger's objection never becomes a marker others might honour.
refusal.not_filed_against_actor: The row is filed where the fold does not look for it, so it would be stored, durable and permanently inert. A marker nobody can find is not a marker.
refusal.not_governed: This community declares no reverse-quorum policy, so it has not adopted the objection plane. Refused rather than defaulted: inventing a window and a threshold for a group that declared neither is worse than saying no.
refusal.not_owner: The commons surface requires the owner (SYSTEM_ADMIN) role.
refusal.objection_absent: objection_id is required: a ballot answers a question about ONE objection.
refusal.objection_unknown: The named objection is not one this node holds against this action.
refusal.session_absent: No session token was presented. The commons surface is owner-only.
refusal.session_invalid: That session is invalid or expired.
refusal.sign_failed: This node could not sign the row, so nothing was submitted.
refusal.steward_tier_not_adopted: This community declared no steward tier, so there is no deadline to be silent past and no escalated pool. A ballot here would be stored and never read.
refusal.store_unavailable: The substrate could not be reached.
refusal.target_action_unknown: The objected-to action is not a row this node holds, so the objection would be uncountable and its window unresolvable.
refusal.unverifiable_signature: The row's signature did not verify against the signer's keys as registered on this node.
refusal.stamped_envelope_mismatch: the echoed `stamped_envelope` does not describe the dismissal in this request. Re-run the dry run for THESE fields and have the co-signers sign what it returns.
refusal.stamped_envelope_required: co-signatures were supplied without the `stamped_envelope` they were made over. Run the dry run, have the co-signers sign the `envelope` it returns, and send that envelope back with their scrubs — otherwise their signatures cover bytes this submission does not carry and the quorum silently counts one.

standing.action_unknown: This node holds no such action. An objection names a row, and there is no row here to name.
standing.cohort_unknown: That cohort does not resolve on this node, so it has no roster and no declaration this node can read. Authority must come from local verified state.
standing.not_governed: This community declares no reverse-quorum policy, so the objection plane does not apply to its commons at all. That is different from nobody having objected.
standing.objected: At least one member has objected and the window is still open. The action stands for now; one more objection may be all it takes.
standing.quiet: The plane was read and no objection has been raised against this action.
standing.reversed: Enough distinct members objected inside the window. Every node holding these rows folds to this same answer, with no coordination.
standing.stood: The window closed below the reversal threshold. This action was objected to and stands.
standing.unreadable: The objection plane could not be read here. This is NOT a statement that nobody objected — the objections are unknown, not absent.

steward.awaiting: The deadline has not passed. The appointed moderators may still answer.
steward.no_duty_holders: A steward tier is declared and this node resolves no appointed moderator for it. Nobody was silent, because nobody was there.
steward.not_adopted: No steward tier was declared, so no moderator deadline applies.
steward.overruled: The appointed moderators ruled that this objection does not stand — and escalation opens anyway, because an undo is never theirs alone to make.
steward.silent: The deadline passed with no ruling either way.
steward.upheld: The appointed moderators ruled, in time, that this objection stands. The matter was judged by named people, on the record.

cost.no_capability_services: You cannot use streams or services that require third-party capability attestations, because you will not have any.
cost.no_reputation: You build NO reputation — every capacity:* claim about you is refused, so none can ever exist.
cost.peers_may_refuse: Some peers may refuse to interact with you at all.

decline_analyze.summary: You may send traces without consenting to be analyzed. Traces will still flow.

analyze.permits: The peer may SCORE your traces — this is what builds reputation.
analyze.title: Be scored

replication.permits: The peer may HOLD your traces.
replication.title: Send traces

grants.independent: These are separate consents on opposite edges. Granting one does not grant the other, and either can be withdrawn without the other.

consent.grant_not_owner_authored: This node wrote that consent before you signed it, so it isn't yours to withdraw here, and the node will not withdraw consent on your behalf. It is still active.
consent.delegate_may_not_withdraw: A delegated session can't withdraw the owner's consent. The withdrawal is signed with the owner's own key.
consent.author_signer_unavailable: Withdrawing consent is signed by the person who gave it, and this node can't use that identity right now. Nothing was withdrawn.
consent.withdraw_failed: The withdrawal could not be stored. Nothing was withdrawn.
consent.delegation_denied: This session's delegation does not grant that action.
consent.malformed_body: The request did not name a grant to withdraw.
consent.store_unavailable: The node could not read its consent records. Nothing was withdrawn. Try again once the node is healthy.
consent.grant_not_live: That is not a live consent grant on this node. It may already be withdrawn.

cost.no_regional_community: You cannot take part in any regional community. Membership is decided by whether your cell falls inside the community's own region, so without a cell there is nothing to compare.
cost.no_regional_reporting: Your activity cannot contribute to regional pattern reporting.

location.permits: Attaches a coarse H3 cell to your envelope so patterns can be reported across regions. The substrate refuses anything finer than resolution 7, so it identifies a rough region — never your specific locality or address.
location.purpose: Regional pattern reporting, and taking part in regional communities. A community may also use it as an OPTIONAL visibility gate, restricting items destined for that community to members whose region falls inside it. It is not a general restriction on your traces — that is decided by the consents above.
location.title: Share your approximate region

mesh.announce_requirement: A node that does not announce gets no service access on the mesh and no agent services. The accord's kill switch is only meaningful against a node it can reach, so an unreachable node is never served in the first place.

private_groups.description: Groups whose addresses are derived from directory state and never announced — membership is anonymous at the scope you choose, and cryptographically opaque to node operators at rest (CC 5.4.6). The substrate side is armed; the surface arrives with the edge v18 adoption.
private_groups.title: Private Groups

video.description: Live audio and video over the mesh itself — session join, subscribe, and publish ride the same verified spine as everything else, keyed end to end, healing mid-stream without dropping a frame. Proven in the edge v18 line; the node-side surface arrives with its adoption.
video.title: Video

voting.description: The full ballot plane: M-of-N accord thresholds verified at the wire, and quorum-above-time ordering in the substrate. The Commons' objection ballots already ship — this is voting as a first-class, verifiable primitive.
voting.title: Voting

consumption.elsewhere: No loop in this build reads this key — its consumer lives in another component. A row set here is admitted and folded, and changes nothing on this node.
consumption.unbuilt: This key's consumer has not been built anywhere yet. A row set here is admitted and folded, and changes nothing.
consumption.unreachable: This key's consumer runs in this process, but nothing carries a value from this plane to it: the component that owns the knob takes it once when the loop is composed and offers no way to change it afterwards. A row set here is admitted and folded, and changes nothing anywhere.
consumption.wired: A loop in this build reads this key and changes what it does. The effective value beside it is in force on this node.

mesh_config.dry_run: Nothing was signed and nothing was submitted. These are the exact canonical bytes a co-signer must sign for their scrub to count on the real submission.

durability.substrate_decides: Which acts earn a durable setting is the substrate's ruling, re-read on every call and reported by its own refusal token. This node encodes no durability rule of its own.

emergency.bound: Emergency relief expires by construction. The maximum window is the substrate's, carried here so a form can bound its input; the substrate refuses anything longer at its own door.

history.empty: Every subscribed root was read and none has ever filed a mesh-config row.
history.no_subscription: This node holds no live trust-root edge, so no root has ever been able to file a mesh-config row here.
history.partial: Some subscribed roots could not be read, so this history is incomplete. The roots that failed are named.
history.present: Every mesh-config row this node holds, newest first.
history.truncated: This page was cut at the limit. The total below counts every row read.
history.unreadable: The mesh-config history could not be read here. This is NOT a statement that no row was ever filed.

outcome.admitted: The substrate admitted this row. It is a MARKER, not a command: nothing was changed by its arrival, and its effect is entirely the read-time fold a consumer may honour.

plane.configured: At least one key is moved off the owner's baseline by a subscribed root.
plane.no_rows_held: This node subscribes to at least one trust root and holds no mesh-config row from any of them. Every key runs at the owner's own baseline.
plane.no_subscription: This node holds no live trust-root edge, so no root may configure it. The subscription IS the trust edge.
plane.none_binding: Mesh-config rows are held and none of them binds: each is expired, clamped to the owner's consent, or asks for the baseline value already in force.
plane.unreadable: The mesh-config plane could not be read here. This is NOT a statement that nothing is set — the values below are unknown, not defaults.

provenance.baseline_not_moved: Subscribed roots hold live rows for this key and none of them moved it: each was clamped to the owner's consent or asked for the value already in force.
provenance.baseline_unspoken: No subscribed root holds a live row for this key, so the node runs the value its owner consented to.
provenance.root: A subscribed root's signed row set this value. The row, its author and the delegation it was taken under are named beside it.

refusal.attribution_absent: delegation_id is required. An act that does not carry its own authority cannot be told from an unauthorized one once the actor is gone.
refusal.authority_not_a_delegation: The named delegation id is not a delegates_to row.
refusal.authority_unresolved: The named delegation is not a row this node holds, so the authority it records would name nothing. Whether it actually authorizes this act is the substrate's ruling, made at its own door.
refusal.grounds_absent: grounds is required. A knob turned for no recorded reason is indistinguishable from one turned for a bad one.
refusal.node_unowned: This node has no responsible party (owner-binding), so it neither reports nor changes mesh configuration on anyone's behalf. Claim ownership first.
refusal.not_owner: The mesh-configuration surface requires the owner (SYSTEM_ADMIN) role.
refusal.root_absent: root_ref is required: a mesh-config row is issued under a trust root, and a row that names none is filed where no fold will ever count it.
refusal.session_absent: No session token was presented. The mesh-configuration surface is owner-only.
refusal.session_invalid: That session is invalid or expired.

ttl.expired: This row's window has closed. The fold drops an expired row at read time, so it needs no revocation and no reachable author.
ttl.running: This row's window is open and closes at the named instant.
ttl.unbounded: This row carries no expiry. It applies until it is superseded.

ladder.attesting_keys_count: {count} keys selected — this is ONE act, with one hash and one reason covering all of them.
ladder.attesting_keys_hint: Paste one key per line (commas or spaces work too)
ladder.attribution_hint: Both are mandatory and both are written into the signed tombstone. An action that does not carry its own authority cannot be told from an unauthorized one once the actor is gone.
ladder.commit_blocked: A delegation id and a reason are required; a quarantine also needs a community id.
ladder.community_id_hint: A quarantine is filed under a community's authority, and a marker that names no community names no authority.
ladder.confirm_quorum: {count} authority chains presented; {min} distinct roots are required.
ladder.confirm_revoked_after: Statements are stood behind up to {at}.
ladder.confirm_title: What you are about to sign
ladder.descent_refused: The payload descent did not run: {token}
ladder.gate_armed: The de-admission gate is armed: this node's own de-admissions are what the substrate compares writers against.
ladder.gate_dormant: The de-admission gate is DORMANT. This node declared no identity to the substrate, so a de-admission written here would refuse nothing.
ladder.gate_foreign_identity: The de-admission gate compares writers against a DIFFERENT key than this node signs as, so a de-admission signed here would never be folded as this node's own.
ladder.gate_unknown: This node reported a de-admission gate state this app does not recognise.
ladder.hash_mismatch_hint: The selection changed between the preview and this signature. The preview that is current has been loaded above — read it before signing again.
ladder.intro: The owner-gated recourse against an admitted peer, graded across tiers 0 to 4. Every rung is preview first, then sign the hash that preview returned — what you were shown is what executes, and a selection that changed in between is refused. Each rung states what it reaches AND what it does not; read both before you sign.
ladder.irreversible_flag: Irreversible. There is no reversal op for this rung.
ladder.limits_unavailable: This app could not load the node's own statement of what this reaches. The limit still applies — the response will state it.
ladder.no_preview_no_commit: Nothing can be signed until a preview has run: the commit presents the hash the preview returned.

ingest.background: Refusals are present but not sustained from a stable identity set: ordinary probes, stale clients and churn. Read `distinct_signers` and `unattributed_in_window` before dismissing it — a HIGH rate spread across a WIDE identity set is a probe, and a HIGH rate that named almost nobody is malformed traffic with a stale client mixed into it. Neither is churn, and neither has one producer to go fix, which is why they read here rather than as a stuck producer.
ingest.clean: Batches were offered to the HTTP ingest path and none was refused inside the window. `refused_total` beside this is the whole-process count: a clean window on a process that refused earlier is a recovery, not an absence.
ingest.http_path_only: This reading covers the HTTP ingest path only. A batch that arrives over the Reticulum relay is verified by the same persist gate but is not counted here, so a clean ingest reading is not a statement about every way a trace can be offered to this node.
ingest.not_exercised: Nothing has been offered to the HTTP ingest path on this process — no batch accepted and none refused. The zero is untested, not clean.
ingest.stuck_producer: A SUSTAINED rate of refusals from a SMALL, STABLE set of signers: a producer is stuck in a retry loop and cannot self-correct. Every one of these refusals is correct — the gate is working — which is exactly why the aggregate needs its own reading. `top_signers` names who to go fix.
ingest.unattributed: Batches were refused and NOT ONE named a signer: they failed before there was an identity to record — malformed bytes, a bad signature, an unsupported schema version. There is no producer to call, and this is deliberately not reported as a stuck producer: zero distinct signers is not a small stable identity set.
ingest.unreadable: This node's ingest refusal ledger could not be read, so nothing here is a statement about what it refused. This is not 'nothing was refused' — it is 'we could not ask'.

key_statements.stands: No revocation this node holds covers a statement made right now.
key_statements.suspect_after_bound: A history-BOUNDED revocation covers a statement made right now: this key is de-admitted as of now, and its honest past still stands. That bound is materially better than an unbounded revocation and does not read the same.
key_statements.suspect_unbounded: An UNBOUNDED revocation covers this key, so everything it ever said is in doubt — the revocation declined to say otherwise.
key_statements.unreadable: This node's key standing could not be computed. That is not 'stands' — an unasked question has no answer.

peer_quota.denials: The peer-write quota recorded slot denials. The tracked-peers cap derivation no longer holds in this build.
peer_quota.no_quota: This backend holds no peer-write quota, so the tripwire reports nothing. That is not a clean reading.
peer_quota.not_exercised: No peer write has been charged against the quota on this process, so its zero is untested rather than clean.

quarantine.not_quarantined: No quarantine marker about this node's key has ever taken effect here.
quarantine.released: This node's key was withheld and then released. It serves now, and it did not always — a different fact from never having been withheld.
quarantine.unreadable: The quarantine state could not be read. That is not 'not quarantined'.
quarantine.withheld: This node's key is withheld from serving by a quarantine marker.

receive.applying: Rows a peer offered were admitted here and changed this node's state, and none was refused. `applied_by_kind` names the planes that moved; `duplicate_total` beside it counts the offered rows this node already held.
receive.converged: Peers offered rows and this node already held every one of them, so nothing changed state and nothing was refused. This is anti-entropy at rest — traffic is arriving and there is nothing left to learn from it.
receive.decided_denominator: `decided_total` is every row a peer offered that reached an apply decision here: applied plus duplicate plus refused. Bytes this node could not decode reach no decision and are counted nowhere, so they are missing from this total rather than folded into it.
receive.idle: Replication rounds finished and no peer offered this node a single row: nothing was applied, nothing was already held, nothing was refused. Its peers had nothing for it, which is not the same fact as having applied everything they sent.
receive.not_exercised: No replication round has finished on this process, so nothing has been offered to this node's apply path. The zero is untested, not clean.
receive.refusing: This node refused rows its peers offered. `apply_refusals_by_kind` names the plane; `key_apply_refusals_by_reason` names the policy token that refused a key.
receive.unreadable: This node's apply counters could not be read, so nothing here is a statement about what it accepted. This is not 'nothing was refused' — it is 'we could not ask'.

edge_metrics.unavailable: This node's carriage counters could not be read, so nothing here describes what it served, withheld, or refused to apply.

ingest_refusals.unavailable: This node's ingest refusal ledger could not be read, so nothing here describes what the admission gate refused. A gate with no reader is what let 8,631 correct refusals a day run unnoticed for 71 hours.

node_state.unavailable: This node's state signals could not be read from the substrate, so nothing here describes its trust root, key standing, quarantine, consent SLA or peer quota. Absence of bad news from an unread source is not good news.

trace_corpus.unavailable: This node's trace corpus could not be read, so nothing here describes what it has admitted. Absence of arrivals from an unread corpus is not absence of arrivals.

trace_plane.dark: NOTHING HAS BEEN ADMITTED FOR LONGER THAN THIS NODE'S RED THRESHOLD. Arrival is the single thing this node exists to do. Read the `ingest` reading beside this: a dark plane with a sustained refusal rate is a producer being correctly rejected, and a dark plane with no refusals at all means nothing is even reaching this node.
trace_plane.future_dated: The newest trace in the corpus is stamped in the FUTURE. The timestamp is the producer's own broadcast clock, so this is a statement about that clock — and it is called out rather than banded because a future-dated row pins this reading green indefinitely and would hide a plane that has actually stopped.
trace_plane.live: A trace was admitted recently: the plane this node exists to receive on is being fed.
trace_plane.never_admitted: The corpus was read and holds no trace at all: nothing has ever been admitted on this node. There is no arrival instant to band, so this is an untested zero, not a healthy one — and on a node that has been serving for a while it is the same condition as a dark plane.
trace_plane.producer_asserted_ts: `last_admitted_at` is MAX(trace_events.admitted_at) — when THIS node last accepted a trace, on its own clock (CIRISPersist#606, persist v32.1.0). It is no longer the producer's assertion, so a peer with a skewed clock can no longer move this node's liveness reading. `None` on a corpus whose rows all predate the admission column: that reads as `never_admitted`, which is honest — this node cannot say when it last accepted one — and deliberately NOT a fallback to the producer's timestamp, which would reinstate the very coupling this replaced. A far-future row is still called out as `future_dated`.
trace_plane.quiet: No trace has been admitted for longer than expected, but not yet long enough to call the plane dark. A genuinely idle node reads this way; so does the first half of a producer outage.
trace_plane.unreadable: This node's trace corpus could not be read, so nothing here is a statement about what it has admitted. This is not 'no trace has arrived' — it is 'we could not ask'.

trust_root.no_self_key: The host never declared this node's own key id, so nothing self-scoped could be walked. This is a statement about the reader, not about the node: declare the key at startup and every self-scoped signal below becomes answerable.
trust_root.no_trust_edges: This node declared itself and holds no live trust edge to any root: it roots to nothing. A known bad, not a missing reading.
trust_root.no_valid_root: This node trusts one or more roots and none of them validates. The per-leg verdict beside this names which leg failed.
trust_root.unreadable: The trust-root walk could not be read. An unreadable directory is not an untrusted one — do not read this as a rootless node.
trust_root.valid: This node roots to a trust root that checks out in full: a live trust edge, a self-declaring charter with a recovery commitment, and no halt latched.

volatility.clock_dependent_local: This band is computed on THIS node from a stored instant against the read clock, so it moves on elapsed time alone — no state change, no new row. A node that stops admitting traces walks green to yellow to red on its own, which is the point: it goes red without anyone asking it to.
volatility.process_local: The carriage, receive and ingest counters are process-local and cumulative since this process started. They reset on restart, differ between processes serving one node, and are stored nowhere. They are a gauge of this process, not a ledger of this node.

withhold_class.fault: A read or a wiring step failed and the serve path failed closed. This is NOT a verdict about the peer — it is this node's fault to fix.
withhold_class.integrity: A row this node holds could not be served at all: it would not serialize, its stored hash would not decode, or advertised bytes were unfetchable. A defect in local state, not a policy.
withhold_class.policy: A decision this node made on purpose — consent scope, a serve capability the peer does not hold, or the producer's own restriction. Working as configured: change the configuration, not the code.
